channel.title: Popcorn Tales
channel.description:
Stories for kids to enjoy together! Popcorn the little owl opens and closes every episode: adventures, animal fables, funny stories, retold classics, bedtime stories and gently spooky tales with friendly ghosts and happy endings. Soft narration and calm sounds for children aged 3 to 7 to listen to with their family. Original stories and public-domain classics retold; every episode is also available in Portuguese on the Pipoca Conta podcast.
Disclosure: narration uses a synthetic (AI-generated) voice. Stories, characters, music and jingle are original to Pipoca Conta.

item.title: Hansel and Gretel and the Cookie House
item.itunes:title: Hansel and Gretel and the Cookie House
item.description:
Two siblings, a great big forest and a house made of cookies... Tonight Popcorn tells the classic Hansel and Gretel in a gentle, loving version with a happy ending, just right for bedtime. 🍪🦉

Hansel and Gretel go into the forest with their woodcutter father and get lost picking blackberries. White pebbles that shine in the moonlight lead them home, but the second time the birds eat the breadcrumbs. With Popcorn the owl, the children spend the night under an oak tree, and in the morning a snow-white bird leads them to a cookie house with an iced roof and sugar windows. It belongs to a grumpy old neighbour who never shared anything, until the day the children take care of her by the oven. A gentle retelling of the Brothers Grimm classic, with no witch, no harsh scares, and a happy ending.

💛 Lesson: brothers and sisters look after each other, calm and clever thinking help us find the way, and everything is sweeter when we share.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7
📖 Source: the Brothers Grimm, "Hansel and Gretel" (Children's and Household Tales no. 15, 1812), public domain. Original kid-friendly retelling by Popcorn Tales, written from the original tale. Nothing copied from films, cartoons or modern copyrighted versions. The hard parts of the original were softened for little ones: the children get lost by accident, there is no witch and no cage, nobody is pushed into the oven and nobody gets hurt; the owner of the house learns to share.

At Popcorn Tales, Popcorn the owl opens and closes every story. Soft narration, watercolor art, and calm sound. Also in Portuguese on Pipoca Conta.

🎵 Music: original score and jingle by Popcorn Tales. Sound effects public domain/CC0 (Wikimedia Commons) and synthesized.
🤖 Narrated with a synthetic (AI-generated) voice. Original story and characters.

▶️ Video version: https://youtu.be/HfR0iTiQm00

item.title: The Boy Who Didn't Know Fear
item.itunes:title: The Boy Who Didn't Know Fear
item.description:
A boy set out into the world to learn what fear was... Tonight Popcorn tells a gentle, funny spooky story for kids, with a happy ending, just right for a special night. 👻🦉

Bruno did not know what fear was. With Popcorn the owl, he walks through the moonlit forest, meets a bell ringer wrapped in a white blanket, and spends the night in a castle that everyone left because of rumors. Inside, cats and a dog play skittles, a magic bed walks by itself, and what seemed scary turns into a surprise. In the end, a playful splash of fresh water teaches Bruno what a shiver feels like, and everybody laughs. A gentle retelling of the Brothers Grimm classic, with no harsh scares, no real danger, and a happy ending.

💛 Lesson: when we look closely, with courage and kindness, many things that seem scary turn into a funny surprise, and fear grows smaller.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7
📖 Source: the Brothers Grimm, "The Story of the Youth Who Went Forth to Learn What Fear Was" (Children's and Household Tales no. 4, 1812), public domain. Original kid-friendly retelling by Popcorn Tales, written from the original tale. Nothing copied from films, cartoons or modern copyrighted versions; the boy is named Bruno, the princess and the bell ringer have no film names, and the hard parts of the original were softened for little ones.

At Popcorn Tales, Popcorn the owl opens and closes every story. Soft narration, watercolor art, and calm moonlight sound. Also in Portuguese on Pipoca Conta.

🎵 Music: original score and jingle by Popcorn Tales. Sound effects public domain/CC0 (Wikimedia Commons) and synthesized.
🤖 Narrated with a synthetic (AI-generated) voice. Original story and characters.

item.title: Sleeping Beauty and the Castle of Roses
item.itunes:title: Sleeping Beauty and the Castle of Roses
item.description:
A princess, twelve golden plates, and one fairy who was forgotten... Tonight Popcorn tells the famous fairy tale of Sleeping Beauty, slowly and softly, just right for bedtime. 🌹🦉

When the princess is born, the king throws a great feast and invites twelve fairies, but he forgets the thirteenth. Hurt, the forgotten fairy casts a spell: at fifteen, the princess will prick her finger on a spinning wheel and fall into a deep sleep. The youngest fairy makes the spell gentler: the whole castle will sleep together with her until the right day to wake up. A hundred years later, a hedge of roses opens for a kind prince, and Popcorn the owl shows him the way to the tower. A gentle version with no scares, with a peaceful awakening, an apology, forgiveness and a happy ending.

💛 Lesson: nobody should be left out: remembering everyone keeps hearts happy, and forgiveness can turn even a spell into a happy ending.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7
📖 Source: Charles Perrault, "The Sleeping Beauty in the Wood" (1697), and the Brothers Grimm, "Dornröschen" (Children's and Household Tales no. 50, 1812), both public domain. Original kid-friendly retelling by Popcorn Tales, written from the original tales. Nothing copied from films, cartoons or modern copyrighted versions; the princess, the fairies, the prince, the king and the queen have no names on purpose. The spell is only a sleeping spell, and the hard parts of the originals were softened for little ones.

At Popcorn Tales, Popcorn the owl opens and closes every story. Soft narration, watercolor art, and calm sound. Also in Portuguese on Pipoca Conta.

🎵 Music: original score and jingle by Popcorn Tales. Sound effects public domain/CC0 (Wikimedia Commons) and synthesized.
🤖 Narrated with a synthetic (AI-generated) voice. Original story and characters.

item.title: Rapunzel and the Tower in the Woods
item.itunes:title: Rapunzel and the Tower in the Woods
item.description:
Rapunzel, Rapunzel, let down your hair... Tonight Popcorn tells the famous fairy tale of Rapunzel, the girl in the tower with no door. 🏰🦉

Rapunzel grew up with a very jealous enchantress, who kept her in a tall tower in the middle of the forest, with no door and no stairs. The only way up is the girl's long golden braid! With the friendship of Popcorn the owl and a kind prince who falls in love with her singing, Rapunzel weaves a silk ladder and dreams of seeing the world. But the enchantress discovers the secret... Will the two friends find each other again? A gentle version with no scares, with a reunion, forgiveness and a happy ending.

💛 Lesson: true love never locks anyone away: it cares, it trusts, and it lets us fly; and forgiving makes our hearts light.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7
📖 Source: Brothers Grimm, "Rapunzel" (Children's and Household Tales no. 12, 1812, with details from the 1857 edition, public domain). Original kid-friendly retelling by Popcorn Tales, written from the original tale. Nothing copied from films, cartoons or modern copyrighted versions; the enchantress, the prince and the parents have no names on purpose. The hard parts of the original were softened for little ones.

At Popcorn Tales, Popcorn the owl opens and closes every story. Soft narration, watercolor art, and calm sound. Also in Portuguese on Pipoca Conta.

🎵 Music: original score and jingle by Popcorn Tales. Sound effects public domain/CC0 (Wikimedia Commons) and synthesized.

item.title: Cinderella and the Glass Slipper
item.itunes:title: Cinderella and the Glass Slipper
item.description:
When the clock strikes midnight, the magic will end... Tonight Popcorn tells the famous fairy tale of Cinderella and the Glass Slipper. 👠🦉

Cinderella is the kindest girl in town, even though she works all day beside the ashes of the fireplace. With help from little owl Popcorn, the garden birds and a fairy godmother, a pumpkin becomes a carriage and she goes to the grand ball at the palace. But at midnight, a glass slipper is left behind on the staircase... Will the prince find the owner of the slipper? A gentle version with no scares, with forgiveness and a happy ending.

💛 Lesson: kindness and forgiveness make our hearts light, and gentleness always finds its way.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7
📖 Source: Charles Perrault, "Cendrillon ou la petite pantoufle de verre" (Cinderella, or the Little Glass Slipper, 1697, public domain), with one detail from the Brothers Grimm tale "Aschenputtel" (Children's and Household Tales no. 21, 1812, public domain). Original kid-friendly retelling by Popcorn Tales, written from the original tales. Nothing copied from films, cartoons or modern copyrighted versions; the stepmother, the stepsisters and the mice have no names on purpose.

At Popcorn Tales, little owl Popcorn opens and closes every story. Soft narration, watercolor art, and calm sound. Also in Portuguese on Pipoca Conta.

🎵 Music: original score and jingle by Popcorn Tales. Sound effects public domain/CC0 (Wikimedia Commons) and synthesized.
🤖 Narrated with a synthetic (AI-generated) voice. Original story and characters.

item.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
item.itunes:title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
item.description:
Mirror, little mirror... who is the fairest of them all? Tonight Popcorn tells the famous fairy tale of Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs. 🍎🦉

Snow White has the kindest heart in the kingdom, and the vain queen grows very jealous. In the dark forest, little owl Popcorn guides the princess to the cottage of the seven dwarf miners. But an old woman arrives with an enchanted apple... Will Snow White wake up from her enchanted sleep? A gentle version with no big scares and a happy ending.

💛 Lesson: true beauty lives in a kind heart; envy only makes us sad, and good friends keep us safe.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7
📖 Source: Brothers Grimm, "Schneewittchen" (Snow White), Children's and Household Tales no. 53 (1812, public domain). Original kid-friendly retelling by Popcorn Tales, written from the Grimm tale. Nothing copied from films, cartoons or modern copyrighted versions; the dwarfs have no names on purpose.

At Popcorn Tales, little owl Popcorn opens and closes every story. Soft narration, watercolor art, and calm sound. Also in Portuguese on Pipoca Conta.

🎵 Music: original score and jingle by Popcorn Tales. Sound effects public domain/CC0 (Wikimedia Commons) and synthesized.

item.title: The Cloud Who Couldn't Fall Asleep
item.itunes:title: The Cloud Who Couldn't Fall Asleep
item.description:
A restless little cloud, a sky full of friends, and a soft rain that rocks her to sleep... Tonight Popcorn helps Cotton find her rest. ☁️🌙

Cotton just can't close her eyes. With Popcorn the little owl, she asks the Moon, the Wind and the little stars how to fall asleep. Breathe deeply, float with no hurry, and count the lights in the sky... until a gentle rain rocks the little cloud and sleep arrives very quietly.

💛 Lesson: calm your body and mind; it's okay to slow down.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7 years

item.title: Popcorn's Trip Through the Planets
item.itunes:title: Popcorn's Trip Through the Planets
item.description:
A cardboard box, a little imagination and... lift off! Tonight Popcorn takes Lara on a trip through every planet in the Solar System. 🚀🪐

Lara can't fall asleep, and through her window she sees a little light shining brighter than all the stars. Popcorn the little owl tells her it's the planet Venus! With help from Boris the little ghost, they turn a cardboard box into a rocket and visit Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, discovering fun facts about each one: the hottest planet, Jupiter's giant storm, the planet that would float in a bathtub and the one that spins on its side. At the end, back in bed, Lara counts the planets very slowly until she falls asleep.

💛 Lesson: curiosity is like a rocket: every question takes us on a brand new adventure.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7 years
📖 Source: an original Popcorn Tales story, with simple science facts about the Solar System.
🔭 Planet photos: NASA / JPL-Caltech / Johns Hopkins APL / USGS / Space Science Institute / ESA (public domain, via Wikimedia Commons).

On Popcorn Tales, Popcorn the little owl opens and closes every story. Soft narration, illustrations and calm sounds for bedtime. Also in Portuguese on Pipoca Conta.

item.title: The Princess and the Magic Pea
item.itunes:title: The Princess and the Magic Pea
item.description:
Time to snuggle up for a bedtime story with Popcorn the owl! 🌙

On a rainy night, Princess Nina and her tiny owl Popcorn knock on a castle door. Kind Queen Dorothy makes a bed of ten mattresses… and hides a very special pea at the bottom. Will Nina be able to sleep? And what will she say in the morning? A gentle story, with a part where we count the mattresses together.

💛 Lesson: telling the truth kindly is a beautiful thing, and a calm heart helps us fall asleep.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7 years
📖 Source: an original retelling of the classic fairy tale "The Princess and the Pea" by Hans Christian Andersen (1835, public domain).

item.title: The Little Ghost Who Was Scared of People
item.itunes:title: The Little Ghost Who Was Scared of People
item.description:
Creaks in the attic, a little round shadow in the hallway... who could it be? A gently spooky story with a warm, cozy ending for bedtime! 🌙

Lara has just moved into a blue house on top of a hill, and she's a tiny bit afraid of the dark. At night, she hears creaks and little footsteps up in the attic. With a flashlight in her hands and Popcorn the little owl on her shoulder, she climbs the stairs to find out... and meets Boris, a teeny tiny ghost who is very scared of people! A lightly suspenseful story full of giggles, about talking about our fears and making a friend who seems different.

💛 Lesson: when we talk about our fears, they get teeny tiny, and someone who seems different can become a wonderful friend.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7 years
📖 Source: an original Popcorn Tales story (not based on any book or film).

item.title: The Out-of-Tune Road Band
item.itunes:title: The Out-of-Tune Road Band
item.description:
A donkey, a dog, a cat and a rooster form the most out-of-tune band in the world! Time to giggle along with Popcorn! 🌙

Theodore the donkey can't carry sacks of corn anymore, but his voice is still super strong. So he sets off for Flute Town to become a singer! Along the way, Popcorn the little owl, Pitanga the dog, Whiskers the cat and Crispin the rooster join the band. At night, in a forest cabin, they find two greedy raccoons with the town's festival pies... and only a very out-of-tune song can save the day!

💛 Lesson: it's never too late to start again, and together we are much stronger.
👧 Recommended age: 3 to 7 years
📖 Source: a free retelling of "The Town Musicians of Bremen" by the Brothers Grimm (1819, public domain). Names, characters and ending created by Popcorn Tales.

item.description:

In Sunflower Village, every dragon learns to breathe fire... except Bartholomew. Every time he tries, all that comes out is a sneeze of soap bubbles! With help from his friend Mel, Popcorn the little owl and Granny Cotinha, he finds out his bubbles can save the village on a scorching hot day.
